The OSGeo Indonesia website now has a **News** section, and it is open to
anyone in the community.

Until now the site was a set of static pages that only a couple of people
edited. That works for pages like *About* and *Contact*, which rarely change,
but it left nowhere to put the things the community actually produces —
workshop write-ups, tutorials, notes from a mapping day, a report from a
conference someone attended.

## What you can write

Anything useful to the Indonesian open source geospatial community:

- **Event reports** — what happened at a meetup, workshop, or mapathon
- **Tutorials** — how you solved something in QGIS, PostGIS, GeoServer, GRASS
- **Project updates** — progress on something you are building or mapping
- **Conference notes** — takeaways from FOSS4G or FOSS4G Asia
- **Community news** — a new local group, a university adopting open source GIS

English or Bahasa Indonesia are both fine. Write in whichever you think of
first — a good post in one language beats a hesitant one in two.

## You keep the credit

Every post carries an `author` field, and your name appears:

- on the post itself, under the title
- on the [News](../../news.qmd) listing, next to the date
- in the repository's commit history, permanently attached to your GitHub
  account

Every page on this site also has **Edit this page**, **View source**, and
**Report an issue** links in the sidebar. Those point at the exact file on
GitHub, so anyone reading can see who wrote a page, who changed it, and
what each change was. Nothing here is anonymous, and nothing is hidden.

## How to submit

The full walkthrough is in
[CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/osgeoid/osgeoid.github.io/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md),
but the short version:

1. Fork [osgeoid/osgeoid.github.io](https://github.com/osgeoid/osgeoid.github.io)
2. Create `posts/YYYY-MM-DD-your-title/index.qmd`
3. Fill in the front matter — `title`, `description`, `author`, `date`,
   `categories`
4. Write the post in Markdown, put any images alongside it in the same folder
5. Open a pull request

If git is unfamiliar, that is genuinely fine. Write the post in whatever you
normally use and send it to the
[mailing list](https://lists.osgeo.org/mailman/listinfo/indonesia) or the
[Telegram group](https://t.me/osgeoid) — someone will help you get it in, and
the byline still goes to you.

## Why bother with the git workflow

Because it makes authorship real rather than declared. The commit history is
the record: it shows who wrote what, when, and what changed since. That is the
same reason open source geospatial projects work the way they do, and it seems
right that the chapter's own site works that way too.

Looking forward to reading what you write.
